chunks: And it is narrated from one of them (the Imams) who said:
If you have a stay in Madinah for three days, complete the prayer, and likewise in Makkah; and if you stay for three days, complete the prayer.

And if you have a stay in Madinah for three days, fast three days; fast on Wednesday and pray on the night of Wednesday next to the Pillar of Repentance, which is the Pillar of Abu Lubabah, to which he tied himself until his excuse was revealed from the heavens.
And sit by it on Wednesday, then come on the night of Thursday, which follows, next to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and sit by it your night and your day, and fast on Thursday.
Then come to the pillar that is next to the place of the Prophet (peace be upon him) on the night of Friday, and pray by it your night and your day, and fast in it on Friday.

If you can, do not speak anything during these three days except what you must, and do not leave the mosque except for a need, and do not sleep at night or during the day [in night and day], then do so, for it is superior [for that is among that for which excellence is counted].
Then praise Allah on Friday, extol Him, send blessings on the Prophet, and ask for your need.

And let what you say be: O Allah, whatever need I had to You, I hastened in seeking and requesting it, or a need I did not hasten, I asked You for it [or did not ask You for it], for I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), the Prophet of Mercy, in fulfilling my needs, small and large.

key_terms.أَبُو لُبَابَةَ: Abu Lubabah (a companion who tied himself to a pillar)
key_terms.مَقَامَ النَّبِيِّ: Place of the Prophet (referring to his grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ritual and supplication for a three-day visit to Madinah according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* prescribes a rigorous three-day spiritual retreat in Madinah, emphasizing the sanctity of Wednesday through Friday by linking them to the pillar of Abu Lubabah and the Prophet’s resting place. It highlights the Shia tradition of *I'tikaf* (seclusion) within the mosque, advocating for silence, fasting, and wakefulness to maximize spiritual presence. The practice culminates in a supplication seeking needs through the Prophet’s intercession, reflecting the theological importance of *Tawassul* in Shia devotion.
